newsitem.title: USA: Grace staffing unit sees U.S. nursing shortages.
newsitem.headline: Grace staffing unit sees U.S. nursing shortages.

text.p: The head of W.R. Grace & Co unit Cross Country Staffing said on Tuesday that employer demand was steadily increasing for many nursing specialities and that nursing shortages were developing across the United States.
"Demand is outpacing supply," said Joseph Boshart, chief executive of the Grace unit which places nurses and other healthcare workers in temporary assignments.

Boshart told a meeting of reporters the hiring pressures were in select specialties, such as acute care, and were due mainly to a dwindling number of graduates from nursing schools and cost-saving campaigns by managed-care organizations eliminating much in-house training. "People are retiring and no one is replacing them," he said.

Nurses were in very short supply in the late 1980s and early 1990s, with wages increasing at twice the rate of inflation, he said. But, in recent years, nurses have been laid off in great numbers across the United States.
"The shortages will be even more severe this time," Boshart said.

Cross Country is a $124 million-a-year partnership between 60 percent-owner Grace and Nestor-BNA Plc of Britain which supplies nurses and other temporary health workers to hospitals across the United States.
